resources.string: A libxposed API 102 USB module that hooks system_server to show a chooser for USB mode and ADB on every computer connection.
• Detects USB connections automatically (hooks UsbDeviceManager + broadcast fallback)
• Shows the USB chooser on every computer connection (falls back to a full-screen notification intent when background-start is restricted)
• Available modes: Charge only / File transfer (MTP) / Photo transfer (PTP) / USB tethering (RNDIS) / MIDI
• Enables USB debugging (ADB) with a single tap
• No chooser for OTG devices (phone acting as a USB host); handled natively by the system
• Turns ADB off after unplug (can be disabled), ensuring adbd stops
• Logs go to LSPosed: LSPosed Manager → Modules → USBManager → ⋮ menu → View logs
1. Enable this module in LSPosed and tick \"system\" in scope (the system_server scope for API 102)
2. Tap the top \"module active\" banner to verify the hooks; otherwise reboot or run: adb shell killall system_server
3. Connect to a computer via USB; the chooser appears every time (via a full-screen high-priority notification when locked/in the background)
4. Choose the USB mode and ADB toggle, then tap \"OK\" to apply
5. Tap \"Re-check\" on the top status card to re-check module activation
6. Tap \"How to get logs\" to learn how to export the full hook log from LSPosed

Identifies computers through a dedicated USB Authenticate interface. Tap Detect once and approve the request in your root manager. Detection runs entirely on the phone and needs no cable, computer, or companion installation. The app does not request root by default; root is used only for detection, enabled cable sessions, and device management.

How to activate this module in LSPosed

1. Open LSPosed Manager (or its entry in Magisk)

2. Go to the Modules page, find "USB Manager", and open its details

3. Turn on the enable switch in the top-right corner

4. Under Scope, tick "system" (the system_server-specific scope)

5. Go back and choose Reboot, or run:
 adb shell killall system_server

After rebooting, return here and tap "Re-check" — "Module active" means success.

If it still doesn't work, check the module log in LSPosed Manager.

1. Open LSPosed Manager (or the LSPosed module manager)
2. Go to the Modules tab
3. Find USBManager and open its details
4. Tap the ⋮ (more) menu in the top-right corner
5. Tap "View logs" to see the full hook log, including:
 • Whether the module was injected into system_server
 • Each USB plug/unplug event
 • Whether APPLY_USB_CONFIG was received after your choice
 • Whether the mode switch and ADB toggle succeeded

[Alternative: command line]
 adb logcat -c && adb logcat -s USBManager:V LSPosedFramework:V
